land.text: the Estonian SSR, into which 'Estonia was annexed by the Soviet Union' on 6 August 1940; independence was restored on 20 August 1991

predecessors.note: The land the republic governs from 1991.

land.text: the interwar republic, whose 'legal continuity ... was preserved through the government-in-exile'

predecessors.note: One state in law (both Cliopatria rows carry Wikidata Q191), two dossiers here: the Estonian SSR intervenes 1940-1991, and the existing dossier estonia (another batch) ends in August 1940. The two Cliopatria shapes (1919-1939 and 1992-2024) have the identical area, 48,568.9 km2.

correction.text: Estonia in the year the page dates the restoration of independence (20 August 1991): the same outline as Cliopatria's 1992 shape, only the years change

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria starts the Republic in 1992; the page says 'Estonia declared restoration of independence on 20 August 1991' and that the Soviet authorities recognised it on 6 September 1991.

1992-2023, 48,569 km2 against the infobox 45,335 km2 (ratio 1.07). The Border page says 'the administrative boundary became the de facto international border', i.e. the former Soviet boundary, not the Treaty of Tartu line that still included Pechory and the Narva east bank (annexed to the Russian SFSR on 23 August 1944). In the gazetteer the shape equals the modern country (227 of 228 cells; one cell on Lake Peipus falls in Russia), so it correctly leaves those borderlands out. The same polygon is also Cliopatria's 1919-1939 Estonia, which therefore lacks Pechory and Ivangorod (note for the estonia dossier).

2024, identical to the 1992 shape: 'As of May 2021, the treaty had not been ratified by either party' (the 2014 border agreement), so the de facto line of 1991-1995 still holds; the Saatse Boot road was closed in October 2025.

region.text: Estonia within the former Soviet administrative boundary: 'Estonia declared restoration of independence on 20 August 1991'

ledger.note: 1991, 20 August: Estonia declares the restoration of independence. 'Estonia declared restoration of independence on 20 August 1991' after the 'Singing Revolution' of 1988-1990; 'Legal continuity of the Estonian state was preserved through the government-in-exile'. The page gives no boundary; the region is Cliopatria's 1992 shape. The last Russian army units left in 1994 (the page gives no day), which is not drawn as an occupation.

region.text: the whole country, which the Soviet Union held as the Estonian SSR until it recognised independence

ledger.note: 1991, 20 August: independence restored against Soviet rule. The page: 'On 6 August 1940, Estonia was annexed by the Soviet Union as the Estonian SSR'; the restoration of 20 August 1991 opens the last weeks of the contest. The union dossier dates the contest from 30 March 1990, a date this page does not give.
1991, 6 September: the Soviet Union recognises Estonia. 'Soviet authorities recognised Estonian independence on 6 September 1991'; the UN admitted Estonia on 17 September.

wars.name: Singing Revolution
wars.outcome: Independence restored on 20 August 1991 and recognised by the Soviet authorities on 6 September 1991; the sovereignty declaration of 16 November 1988 began it.
wars.note: A non-violent movement ('the 1988-1990 Singing Revolution against Soviet rule'); listed because it is the path from the Soviet republic to the Republic. The Russian army's last units left in 1994.

certainty.note: The Russian frontier follows the former Soviet administrative boundary, the de facto border agreed by 1995; the treaties of 2005 and 2014 were signed but, 'as of May 2021', not ratified by both parties, and Estonia's claim to the Treaty of Tartu line (Pechory, the Narva east bank) is a diplomatic position, not a held territory. The sea and island borders are not discussed on the pages opened.

sources.title: Estonia
sources.note: Identity, capital, area 45,335 km2, Singing Revolution, restoration 20 August 1991, recognition 6 September 1991, legal continuity, Russian troops left 1994, 1944 transfer of about 5 percent of territory.

sources.title: Estonia-Russia border
sources.note: Tartu 1920 line, 23 August 1944 annexation of Pechory and the Narva east bank, de facto border since 1991, agreement by 1995, treaties of 2005 and 2014 unratified.

notes: Two pages opened (budget 1-2). Rows: Cliopatria's 'Estonia' (1919-1939, slug estonia) and 'Republic of Estonia' (1992-2024) both carry Q191 and the same polygon (48,568.9 km2); I treat them as two dossiers of one state in law, because the Estonian SSR (1940-1991, dossier estonian-soviet-socialist-republic) intervenes and the dossier estonia (another batch) already ends in 1940. The restoration doctrine (continuity through the government-in-exile) is in the predecessor note. Not settled: the date of the Soviet-Estonian declaration of 30 March 1990 (the Estonia page does not mention it), the day the last Russian unit left in 1994, the dates of the 2005 and 2014 treaties (the Border page cites 18 February 2014 only in its references), and the status of the islands and the Gulf of Finland sea border. The Pechory/Izborsk district and the Narva east bank (Ivangorod) are outside the 1992 shape and not drawn as Estonia; they would belong to the russian-federation dossier. No ruler list opened. All regions resolve in the gazetteer.
